guide_line: Find a molar mass, then convert grams, moles, and particles in either direction.
steps: A molecular formula counts the atoms in one molecule. An empirical formula is that count divided by the greatest common factor. C4H10O2 reduces to C2H5O.
A subscript belongs to the symbol in front of it. H2 is one bonded molecule. 2H is two separate atoms. Isomers share a molecular formula and differ in how the atoms connect.
Seven elements are commonly diatomic: H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, and I2.

Use these atomic masses at full precision: H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, Na 22.990, Mg 24.305, S 32.06, Cl 35.45. Multiply each mass by its subscript, add, then round to 4 significant figures. Divide grams by the molar mass to get moles. Divide a particle count by 6.022×10^23 to get moles. Multiply when you go the other way.

worked_example.q: What is the molar mass of CH4? Use C 12.011 and H 1.008. Round to 4 significant figures.

similar_problem.q: What is the molar mass of SO2? Use S 32.06 and O 15.999. Round to 4 significant figures.
similar_problem.hint: SO2 is one sulfur and two oxygens. Compute 32.06 + 2(15.999) and round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of H2O? Use H 1.008 and O 15.999. Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Water is H2O. Compute 2(1.008) + 15.999 and round to 4 significant figures, in g/mol.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of CO2? Use C 12.011 and O 15.999. Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Carbon dioxide is one carbon and two oxygens. Compute 12.011 + 2(15.999) and round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of NaCl? Use Na 22.990 and Cl 35.45. Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Sodium chloride is NaCl. Add 22.990 and 35.45. Keep four significant figures, unit g/mol.

problems.q: The molar mass of water is 18.02 g/mol. How many moles are in 36.04 g of water?
problems.why: Moles = mass / molar mass. 36.04 g / 18.02 g/mol = 2.000 mol.
hints: Divide 36.04 g of water by the molar mass 18.02 g/mol.

problems.q: How many molecules are in 0.2500 mol of a compound? Use 6.022×10^23 particles in 1 mol. Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Multiply 0.2500 mol by 6.022×10^23 per mol and round the coefficient to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: A molecule has the formula C4H10O2. What is its empirical formula?
problems.why: The greatest common factor of 4, 10, and 2 is 2. Divide each subscript by 2 to get C2H5O.
hints: Divide each subscript in C4H10O2 by their greatest common factor, 2.

problems.q: A compound has empirical formula NO2 and molar mass 92.02 g/mol. Use N 14.007 and O 15.999. What is the molecular formula?
problems.why: Empirical mass = 14.007 + 2(15.999) = 46.005 g/mol, which is 46.01 g/mol to 4 significant figures. 92.02 / 46.01 = 2, so the molecular formula is N2O4.
hints: The empirical mass of NO2 is 14.007 + 2(15.999), about 46.01 g/mol. Divide 92.02 by that mass and scale NO2 by the whole number.

problems.q: List the seven elements that are commonly found as diatomic molecules. Separate the formulas with commas.
problems.a: H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, I2
problems.why: The seven diatomic elements are H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, and I2.
hints: Start with hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen, then add fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine. Skip S8.

nearMiss.hint: S8 is a sulfur molecule, but sulfur is not one of the seven diatomic elements.

problems.q: The molecular formula of a phosphorus oxide is P4O10. What is its empirical formula?
problems.why: Both subscripts divide by 2. P4O10 reduces to P2O5.
hints: Divide both subscripts in P4O10 by 2 and write the smaller whole-number formula.

problems.q: NaCl has molar mass 58.44 g/mol. What is the mass of 2.500 mol of NaCl? Round to 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Mass = moles × molar mass. 2.500 mol × 58.44 g/mol = 146.1 g.
hints: Multiply 2.500 mol of NaCl by 58.44 g/mol and round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: How many atoms are in 0.1000 mol of an element? Use 6.022×10^23 atoms in 1 mol.
hints: 0.1000 mol is one tenth of 6.022×10^23. The exponent drops from 23 to 22.

problems.q: Which formula means one molecule of hydrogen, two atoms bonded together? Type H2 or 2H.
problems.why: The subscript in H2 means the two hydrogen atoms are bonded in one molecule. 2H means two separate atoms.
hints: A subscript 2 on H means the two atoms are bonded in one molecule. Type H2, not 2H.

problems.q: Two compounds both have formula C3H6O, but the atoms are connected differently. What are these compounds called?
problems.why: Same molecular formula and different connections means the compounds are structural isomers.
hints: The formula C3H6O matches in both compounds, but the bonds do not. Name compounds that share a formula and differ in connections.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of MgCl2? Use Mg 24.305 and Cl 35.45. Round to 4 significant figures.
problems.why: The subscript 2 applies to chlorine. 24.305 + 2(35.45) = 95.205, which rounds to 95.21 g/mol.
hints: MgCl2 has one magnesium and two chlorines. Compute 24.305 + 2(35.45), then round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: How many moles are in 24.02 g of carbon? Use 12.011 g/mol. Round to 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Moles = grams / molar mass. 24.02 g / 12.011 g/mol = 1.9998 mol, which rounds to 2.000 mol.
hints: Divide 24.02 g of carbon by 12.011 g/mol. Multiplying those two numbers goes the wrong way.

problems.q: How many moles is 3.011×10^23 atoms? Use 6.022×10^23 atoms in 1 mol. Round to 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Moles = atom count / Avogadro's number. 3.011×10^23 / 6.022×10^23 = 0.5000 mol.
hints: Divide 3.011×10^23 atoms by 6.022×10^23 per mol. Do not multiply the atom count by that number.

problems.q: How many atoms are in 11.50 g of sodium? Use Na 22.990 g/mol and 6.022×10^23 atoms in 1 mol. Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: First divide 11.50 g by 22.990 g/mol. Then multiply that mole count by 6.022×10^23 and round to 4 significant figures.
